questions.question_text: A university compares the average starting salaries of graduates from Engineering, Science, Commerce, and Arts using samples from each group. Which hypothesis pair is appropriate for a one-way ANOVA?

options.A: H₀: μ₁  μ₂  μ₃  μ₄; Hₐ: All means are equal
options.B: H₀: At least one population mean differs; Hₐ: All population means are equal
options.C: H₀: μ₁ = μ₂ = μ₃ = μ₄; Hₐ: At least one population mean differs
options.D: H₀: μ₁ ≠ μ₂ ≠ μ₃ ≠ μ₄; Hₐ: All population means are equal

questions.explanation: In a one-way ANOVA, the null hypothesis ($H_0$) states that all group population means are equal ($H_0: \mu_1 = \mu_2 = \mu_3 = \mu_4$), while the alternative hypothesis ($H_a$) states that at least one population mean differs from the others.

questions.question_text: A researcher performs a one-way ANOVA to compare the average productivity of employees working under four different training programmes. The null hypothesis is rejected. Which conclusion is most appropriate?

options.A: Every training programme has a significantly different mean productivity from every other programme.
options.B: The training programme with the largest sample mean is the best programme.
options.C: There is sufficient evidence that at least one programme has a different population mean productivity.
options.D: The sample means must all be different because the null hypothesis was rejected.

questions.explanation: Rejecting the null hypothesis in ANOVA indicates statistically significant evidence that at least one group's population mean productivity differs from the others, without specifying which or if all means differ.

questions.question_text: Why is the technique called Analysis of Variance (ANOVA) even though its objective is to compare population means?

options.A: Because ANOVA directly compares the variances of the populations instead of their means.
options.B: Because ANOVA assumes that all population variances are unequal before comparing means.
options.C: Because differences among population means are assessed by analysing the variation present within and between the sample groups.
options.D: Because the sample variances are always equal to the population means during the analysis.

questions.explanation: ANOVA evaluates population means by partitioning total variability into variability between group means and variability within sample groups, comparing these components using an F-test.

questions.question_text: Which of the following situations is most appropriate for applying a one-way ANOVA?

options.A: Determining whether the average income in a single city exceeds ₹8 lakh per year.
options.B: Comparing the proportion of customers preferring online shopping across four regions.
options.C: Estimating the average waiting time at a single hospital using a random sample.
options.D: Comparing the mean customer satisfaction scores across customers using four different mobile service providers.

questions.explanation: One-way ANOVA is designed to compare a continuous quantitative variable (satisfaction scores) across three or more categorical independent groups (four mobile service providers).

questions.question_text: A company wants to compare the average monthly sales generated by sales teams in four different regions. Which statistical method is most appropriate for testing whether the regional average sales are significantly different?
questions.explanation: One-Way ANOVA is the appropriate test when comparing the means of a single continuous outcome variable across three or more independent groups.

questions.question_text: A government evaluates the effectiveness of a welfare scheme across six states by comparing the average household income improvement in each state. In this study, the six states represent:
questions.explanation: In ANOVA terminology, 'State' is the single factor (independent variable), and the six states correspond to the six factor levels, treatments, or populations being compared.

questions.question_text: The primary objective of one-way ANOVA is to determine whether:

options.C: Differences among sample means provide sufficient evidence that at least one population mean is different.
options.D: All observations follow a normal distribution.

questions.explanation: The main objective of a one-way ANOVA is to determine if observed sample mean differences provide statistically significant evidence that at least one population mean differs from the rest.

questions.question_text: Why is ANOVA preferred instead of repeatedly conducting multiple hypothesis tests when several populations are compared?

options.B: ANOVA evaluates all population means simultaneously using a single hypothesis test.
options.C: ANOVA compares population medians instead of means.

questions.explanation: ANOVA tests all population means simultaneously in one test, controlling the family-wise Type I error rate that would inflate if multiple pairwise t-tests were conducted.

questions.question_text: Which of the following situations cannot be addressed directly using the one-way ANOVA discussed in the lecture?

options.A: Comparing average crop yields under four fertilizers.
options.B: Comparing average salaries across three academic disciplines.
options.C: Comparing average productivity across five manufacturing plants.
options.D: Estimating the average salary of employees in a single company.

questions.explanation: One-way ANOVA requires comparing two or more population groups. Estimating a single mean for one company is a one-sample inference problem and cannot be addressed with ANOVA.

questions.question_text: A student concludes that rejection of the null hypothesis implies that every population mean is different. Which statement best evaluates this conclusion?

options.A: It is correct because ANOVA compares all possible pairs.
options.B: It is correct only when there are three populations.
options.C: It is incorrect because rejection only indicates that at least one population mean differs.
options.D: It is incorrect because ANOVA tests variances rather than means.

questions.explanation: Rejection of the null hypothesis in ANOVA indicates that at least one group mean is significantly different from another, not that all group means are distinct from each other.
